notes.human: Ground truth: manual yes/no annotation of each animated motion (motion_caption/ground_truth/realworld_50, identical to annotations.xlsx). This is the reference the paper evaluates against.
notes.gpt35/gpt4: Motion-filter verdict on the MotionGPT caption ("does this caption describe <activity>?"). Majority over the 5 repeated runs used for the published table (prompts_feedback/realworld_50/<model>_step10_{0..4}); *_yes_votes = how many of 5 runs said yes. Positive class = correctly generated motion; the filter keeps "yes".
notes.gpt4_outcome: TP: kept & correct, FP: kept but wrong (escaped filter), TN: rejected & wrong, FN: rejected but actually fine.
notes.human_caption_annotation: The paper's "Human" row is a human judging the MotionGPT captions only; those per-clip labels are not in the repo (prompts_feedback/realworld_50/human is empty), so only the table numbers are exported.
notes.joints: same format as viewer/*.json (T x 22 x 3, metres, y-up, floored, frame-0 pelvis at x=z=0).

published.text: sections/experiment/motion_filter.tex line 53: GPT-4 precision 0.901 vs GPT-3.5 0.706; incorrect sequences 35.5% -> 9.9% after GPT-4 filtering. 400 clips (8 classes x 50), 5 repeated LLM runs, mean +- std.

recomputed_from_raw_verdicts.method: macro over 8 activities per run, mean/std over 5 runs (std = population std, as np.std); replicates feedback_loop_eval.ipynb
